# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Category: Game Mechanic

### I. PLACEMENT & COLORING GAMES
Games where you place objects or color cells based on constraints

#### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate cells

#### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Fill cells with numbers 1-9
- **Nansuke** - Fill cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers in rooms
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill cells with consecutive numbers in rooms
- **Hebi** - Place numbers 1-5 forming snake sequences
- **Kurotto** - Place cells to form continuous black extensions from numbered circles

#### C. Cell Coloring/Shading
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on visibility constraints
- **Usowan** - Color cells based on neighbor counts with one wrong number per region
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells black to form continuous walls
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that must "drop" to fill bottom half
- **Norinori** - Color cells in pairs within regions
- **Nuritwin** - Shade cells in two equal-sized blocks per region
- **LITS** - Color four-cell tetrominoes in each region
- **Tilepaint** - Color tile regions based on diagonal constraints

#### D. Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** - Place black triangles so white areas form rectangles

### II. LINE-DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw or connect lines to form patterns

#### A. Loop/Circuit Games
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form single closed loop
- **Masyu** - Draw loop through all circles with specific turn rules
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Draw loop through white circles with directional constraints
- **Mid-loop** - Draw loop with black circles as midpoints
- **Nagareru** - Draw directional loop through arrow cells with wind effects
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Draw loop alternating between moon/sun cells per room
- **Suraromu** - Draw loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing all gates
- **Yajilin** - Draw loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrow counts

#### B. Path/Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of matching numbers with continuous lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect island circles with bridges (1-2 per pair)
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips using given lengths

#### C. Movement Games
- **Satogaeri** - Move circles to countries, tracking cell distances
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas via straight arrows

### III. REGION/BLOCK DIVISION GAMES
Games where you divide the grid into regions with specific properties

#### A. Shape-Based Division
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles, each containing one number
- **Sashigane** - Divide into L-shaped blocks marked by circles and arrows
- **Chained Block** - Divide into blocks with one number/question mark each
- **Five Cells** - Divide into blocks of exactly 5 cells

#### B. Property-Based Division
- **Fillomino** - Fill cells with numbers, each block size matches its number
- **Double Choco** - Create paired white/gray regions of same shape
- **Evolomino** - Place squares on arrows, each block grows by one square
- **Nurimeizu** - Create maze rooms all painted or all white

#### C. Two-Block Division
- **Norinori** - (also listed above) Two colored cells per region
- **Nuritwin** - (also listed above) Two equal blocks per region

### IV. CONSTRAINT SATISFACTION GAMES
Games with number/cell constraints but variable mechanics

#### A. Black Cell Constraints
- **Heyawake** - Paint cells in rooms with constraints on painted count
- **Choco Banana** - Paint black cells forming rectangles/squares

#### B. Direction/Arrow Constraints
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with — or | marks with length limits per direction

## Secondary Category: Core Interaction Type

### **Numerical** (involves numbers as primary constraint)
Sudoku, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Hebi, Nansuke, Fillomino, Kurotto, Hashiwokakero, Hitori, Kurodoko, Usowan, Masyu, Numberlink, Satogaeri, Yosenabe

### **Geometric** (involves shapes, spatial arrangement, symmetry)
Shakashaka, Sashigane, Chained Block, Double Choco, Evolomino, LITS, Shikaku

### **Spatial Logic** (involves paths, connections, or directional flow)
Slitherlink, Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Yajilin, Pencils, Numberlink

### **Region-Based** (dividing space with constraints on regions)
Shikaku, Sashigane, Fillomino, Double Choco, Five Cells, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Heyawake, Nurimeizu

This taxonomy organizes the 42 games by their primary mechanic while acknowledging that many games combine multiple interaction types.
